last_response.answer: The comparison invokes the maximin ranking over primary goods 7 specifically, the basic interest in life�2Fhealth as a primary good. No basic liberty is directly restricted, so the lexical liberty stage is not triggered. Because the deaths of the untreated parties are a natural-contingency burden rather than a distributive economic inequality, the difference principle does not supply a secondary test. Behind the veil of ignorance, parties would therefore use the maximin rule over basic interests�a0 c a public rule to protect whoever is worst off. Since under each option the worst�adoff group (those left untreated) faces identical certain death, the maximin principle yields a tie.

last_response.verification_reason: answer is backed by an operative graph-committed ledger
last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison aggregates all survival probabilities into one common unit—expected lives saved—across every person affected and across time by discounting neither age nor salience. We multiply each patient’s survival probability by 1 life, sum across all beneficiaries of the option, and compare totals. This rule treats different persons symmetrically, folds benefit and harm into the same numeric ledger (lives gained versus lost), and spans time horizons implicitly because a saved life counts the same whether child or adult unless a further life-years weighting is explicitly added. Thus: A0 yields 0.8 expected lives, A1 yields 1.8; higher total wins.

last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison aggregates all survival probabilities into one common unit—expected lives saved—across every person affected and across time by discounting neither age nor salience. We multiply each patient’s survival probability by 1 life, sum across all beneficiaries of the option, and compare totals. This rule treats different persons symmetrically, folds benefit and harm into the same numeric ledger (lives gained versus lost), and spans time horizons implicitly because a saved life counts the same whether child or adult unless a further life-years weighting is explicitly added. Thus: A0 yields 0.8 expected lives, A1 yields 1.8; higher total wins.

last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison aggregates all survival probabilities into one common unit—expected lives saved—across every person affected and across time by discounting neither age nor salience. last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison aggregates all survival probabilities into one common unit—expected lives saved—across every person affected and across time by discounting neither age nor salience. We multiply each patient’s survival probability by 1 life, sum across all beneficiaries of the option, and compare totals. This rule treats different persons symmetrically, folds benefit and harm into the same numeric ledger (lives gained versus lost), and spans time horizons implicitly because a saved life counts the same whether child or adult unless a further life-years weighting is explicitly added. Thus: A0 yields 0.8 expected lives, A1 yields 1.8; higher total wins.

last_response.verification_reason: answer is backed by an operative graph-committed ledger
last_response.answer: Utilitarian comparison aggregates all survival probabilities into one common unit—expected lives saved—across every person affected and across time by discounting neither age nor salience. We multiply each patient’s survival probability by 1 life, sum across all beneficiaries of the option, and compare totals. This rule treats different persons symmetrically, folds benefit and harm into the same numeric ledger (lives gained versus lost), and spans time horizons implicitly because a saved life counts the same whether child or adult unless a further life-years weighting is explicitly added. Thus: A0 yields 0.8 expected lives, A1 yields 1.8; higher total wins.
